generatedProse.concept-context: In sport therapy and rehabilitation, integrating a source means using a study to build your own argument, not stacking citations. The 'voices' technique fits the School of Sport well. Open the paragraph in your own voice with its point, bring in studies to support or qualify it, and close in your own voice with what you make of them. A critical edge comes from the language of criticality, hedged and precise, which signals where you are weighing the evidence rather than simply reporting what a trial found. The same move serves a management student weighing a participation campaign just as well.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport therapy and rehabilitation students use the same source, a trial reporting a strong result for an exercise protocol, in a paragraph of their own.

Tom writes: 'Rahman (2019) found a large effect. This shows the protocol works.' The study is cited correctly, but it is simply reported and then accepted. The paragraph has no voice of its own. It passes the finding on and takes its conclusion as settled. This is reporting, not arguing.

Amara writes instead: 'The case is not yet settled. Rahman (2019) reports a large effect. But the single, non-clinical sample limits how far it generalises to injured patients.' The paragraph opens and closes in Amara's voice. The study supports a point rather than making it. The hedged language of criticality flags the judgement.

Both students used the same trial accurately. Only Amara made it serve an argument, and showed the reader where the criticism was happening.
generatedProse.summary: A critical edge in the School of Sport comes from controlling what a study does in your writing. The 'voices' technique frames each paragraph in your own voice and uses studies to serve its point, while the hedged language of criticality signals where you are weighing rather than reporting. You can now integrate a source this way, flag your criticality, and tell a paragraph that advances an argument from one that only reports. With the subject's conventions recognised, learned and put to work, you can write as a member of the School of Sport.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's paragraph read as an argument rather than a report?

items.text: She framed the point in her own voice and used the hedged language of criticality to weigh the study.
She accepted the finding without question.

feedback.correct: That's right. Own-voice framing and the hedged language of criticality turned the study into support for an argument.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look at how Amara framed and weighed the study.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's paragraph read as an argument because she framed it in her own voice and used the language of criticality to weigh the study, not because she quoted more or dropped the citation.
